content.comment_body: Hello everyone. I'm facing an issue and would appreciate your advice. Normally, when a button on the [product_name] is pressed, the display turns white and then the backlight dims if there are no interactions. I want to add a logic function to alert users by activating an output and the red background using M29. However, when M29 is used, even if it is set to zero, the screen still dims regardless of button presses. How can I modify the logic so the display backlight works as usual when M29 is zero?
There is no workaround for this. As soon as a backlight flag is implemented in the program, controlling the backlight through keyboard interaction becomes unavailable.
Is it not possible to detect button presses on the [product_name]?

Button presses alone are not recognized in the [product_name] logic. Only a combination of the ESC key and a cursor key (ESC + cursor key) can be detected. In that case, you can add the four cursor keys to the program logic and use a flag for the white backlight.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants are encountering difficulties due to the way program-controlled backlight overrides manual activation via button presses on the [product_name]. When using a flag like M29 for alerts, the typical user experience—where pressing a button restores screen backlight—is disrupted. The device only recognizes key combinations (ESC + cursor key) within its logic, limiting options for restoring normal backlight behavior.
analysis.user_expectations: Users would like the backlight to return to standard operation when the logic flag (M29) is not set, allowing for activation by button presses as per the default settings.
